title: Swift MT101 Coexistence Readiness Diff
description: Evaluates Swift CBPR+ MT101 message-type retirement readiness for the end of FI-to-FI coexistence, when bulk/multiple payment initiation drops MT101 (FIN) in favor of pain.001v9 (ISO 20022 MX). The former 14 November 2026 coexistence end was deferred by Swift on 27 August 2026 and no replacement date has been published, so the countdown below is planning-only against the superseded date. Declare the message format currently in production and a structural self-declared readiness checklist and get a deterministic ready/not-ready verdict plus days to the superseded planning date. Client-side, deterministic, zero PII.

mcp_tool_definition.name: check_mt101_coexistence_readiness
mcp_tool_definition.description: Evaluates Swift CBPR+ MT101 message-type retirement readiness (FI-to-FI bulk/multiple payment initiation) from a caller-declared current message format (MT101 or pain.001v9) and a structural self-declared readiness checklist. The former 2026-11-14 coexistence end was deferred by Swift on 27 August 2026 with no replacement date published. Returns a deterministic ready/not-ready verdict, days_to_deadline computed from that superseded fixed constant and a caller-supplied as_of_date (planning-only), and named readiness gaps. Browser-based, client-side only. Zero PII. Link users to https://ainumbers.co/tools/577-mt101-coexistence-readiness-diff.html for interactive use.

currentMessageFormat.description: Message format currently in production for FI-to-FI bulk payment initiation

asOfDate.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) to evaluate readiness as of

emitsPain001v9Bulk.description: True if the sender's system already emits pain.001v9 for bulk FI-to-FI (only relevant when currentMessageFormat is pain.001v9)

fallbackPathStaged.description: True if a fallback pain.001v9 path is staged (only relevant when currentMessageFormat is MT101)

correspondentConfirmedReceipt.description: True if the correspondent has confirmed it can receive pain.001v9 (only relevant when currentMessageFormat is MT101)

author: PostOakLabs
